nav_state.doc: HEARTBEAT.nav_state. Sequential v2 encoding of the firmware flight-state machine.

mode_source.doc: Who selected the active flight mode.

calib_step.doc: CALIBRATION_STATUS.step — progress update or operator instruction (spec §14.8).

perf_fifo_id.doc: PERF_FIFO.fifo_id — stable ids so rows label regardless of send order (spec §14.8).

xfer_flags.doc: XFER_DATA/XFER_ACK.flags — bitmask carried on the bulk-transfer substrate (docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md). DONE/ABORT terminate a session; NAK requests resend from XFER_ACK.next_offset; EOF marks the final XFER_DATA chunk.

messages.name: HEARTBEAT
messages.doc: ~1 Hz liveness, mode, advertised capabilities, wall-clock stamp.

messages.name: SYSTEM_HEALTH
messages.doc: Firmware health counters. v1: SYSTEM_STATUS origin HEALTH.

messages.name: FLIGHT_MODE
messages.doc: Active flight mode and who selected it. v1: SYSTEM_STATUS origin FLIGHT_MODE.

messages.name: STATUSTEXT
messages.doc: Human-readable status/log line. v1: PACKET_TYPE_LOG.

messages.name: COMMAND_ACK
messages.doc: Acknowledges any command, correlated by (command, req_seq).

messages.name: PING
messages.doc: Round-trip liveness probe.

messages.name: CAPABILITIES
messages.doc: Full capability list, on request at connect (spec §13). msgid_ranges omitted in this cut.

messages.name: TIME_SYNC
messages.doc: NTP-style FC<->GCS clock sync (spec §10). The GCS sends role=REQUEST stamping t1_gcs_tx; the FC replies role=RESPONSE echoing t1 and adding t2_fc_rx (its receive time) and t3_fc_tx (its send time). The GCS captures t4 locally on receipt and computes offset=((t2-t1)+(t3-t4))/2, delay=(t4-t1)-(t3-t2). commanded_offset_ms carries the GCS's filtered correction back to the FC (INT32_MIN = none). For deviations beyond int32 ms (~24.8 days, e.g. a cold-start FC uptime clock vs GCS epoch) the GCS sends role=REQUEST_WIDE with the full 64-bit correction split across commanded_offset_ms (low word) and commanded_offset_hi_ms (high word); the high word trailing-zero-truncates away on the normal int32 path so it costs nothing there. Byte-identical to the firmware time_sync_payload_t; all stamps are milliseconds.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: request sequence, echoed in the response

fields.name: commanded_offset_ms
fields.doc: GCS->FC correction (low 32 bits if REQUEST_WIDE); INT32_MIN = none

fields.name: commanded_offset_hi_ms
fields.doc: high 32 bits of the 64-bit correction; only meaningful when role=REQUEST_WIDE, else 0 (truncated off the wire)

messages.name: IMU_RAW
messages.doc: Full IMU snapshot. v1: PACKET_TYPE_IMU_DATA_FULL (10×f32).

fields.name: sample_time_us
fields.doc: added in v2; old peers ignore it (spec §5.5)

messages.name: IMU_COMPRESSED
messages.doc: Delta IMU vs last IMU_RAW. v1: PACKET_TYPE_IMU_DATA_COMPRESSED (10×f16). NOTE: NavLink has no f16 type (spec §5.1); the 10 half-float bit patterns are carried as u16 and decoded by the application.

fields.name: ref_seq
fields.doc: seq of the IMU_RAW this deltas against

messages.name: ATTITUDE_EULER
messages.doc: Euler attitude + body rates, NED frame.

messages.name: RC_CHANNELS
messages.doc: RC channel values. v1: PACKET_TYPE_RC_CHANNELS (14×u16); v2 widens to 18.

messages.name: MOTOR_TELEMETRY
messages.doc: Per-motor output command. v1: PACKET_TYPE_MOTOR_TELEMETRY (4×f32); v2 allows up to 8.

messages.name: CONTROL_TRACE
messages.doc: 18×f32 PID/loop trace. v1: SYSTEM_STATUS origin PID_ERROR (control_telemetry_t).

messages.name: EST_PERF
messages.doc: Estimator loop timing. v1: SYSTEM_STATUS origin EST_PERF (spec §14.8).

messages.name: PERF_GLOBAL
messages.doc: vaios PERF scheduler/ISR/IPC/heap snapshot. One per report; PERF_TASK/PERF_FIFO share `seq` (spec §14.8).

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: report id shared by all fragments

messages.name: PERF_TASK
messages.doc: One task row; `seq` ties it to a PERF_GLOBAL report. Collect total_tasks of these per seq (spec §14.8).

messages.name: PERF_FIFO
messages.doc: One SPSC FIFO row; collect total_fifos per seq (spec §14.8).

messages.name: PERF_TASKNAME_REQUEST
messages.doc: GCS → FC: resolve one task id to its name (spec §14.8).

messages.name: PERF_TASKNAME
messages.doc: FC → GCS reply; name is NUL-padded char[32] (PERF_TASKNAME_MAX) (spec §14.8).

messages.name: BARO
messages.doc: Barometric sensor (BME280): pressure/temperature/humidity + derived altitude.

messages.name: VERTICAL_STATE
messages.doc: Fused vertical estimate from the VERT 3-state filter (baro + accel + accel bias). altitude/climb_rate are the fused outputs (altitude is absolute/MSL, same reference as BARO); agl is the FC-authoritative height above the ground reference (captured while disarmed, frozen at arm); baro_altitude is the raw sensor altitude carried alongside so the GCS can chart fused-vs-raw. valid=0 until the filter is seeded by the first baro fix. agl_tof is the tilt-compensated rangefinder height, meaningful only while tof_valid=1 (fresh, in range, near level) - it is the AGL source flight_phase and the height mode prefer near the ground. height_state is the packed height-mode status (see control/angle_controller.h): bits0-1 requested mode 0=OFF 1=HOLD 2=LAND, bit2 engaged, bit3 runaway-failed, bit4 landed, bit5 handback, bit6 interlock armed, bit7 blocked. accel_bias is the filter's estimate of the DC error in the vertical accelerometer (m/s/s, positive = reads more UP-acceleration than is real); motor vibration drives this to about -1 on this airframe, so it doubles as a vibration read-out. accel_unhealthy=1 means that estimate hit its authority clamp, so climb_rate is NOT trustworthy and the height mode is vetoed.

messages.name: SYSID_SAMPLE
messages.doc: One chunk of the on-hardware system-ID capture, streamed in response to CMD_SYSID_DUMP. u/gyro are the rate-PID OUTPUT (control effort u, incl. the chirp response — this is the plant-fit input, NOT the setpoint) and the measured gyro rate. u is i16 scaled x1000 (recover native u by /1000); gyro is i16 in 0.1 deg/s. start_index is this chunk's first sample; total/capture_hz/axis are repeated in every chunk so a dropped first chunk doesn't lose the metadata.

messages.name: XFER_INFO
messages.doc: Reply to XFER_OPEN once a session is accepted: advertises the negotiated chunk_size and total_size (0xFFFFFFFF = stream/unknown length). Carries no reliability of its own (the session SM owns that); retransmitted by the FC until the first XFER_ACK is seen. Part of the generic bulk-transfer substrate (docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md).

fields.name: result
fields.doc: open result; ACCEPTED means the rest is valid

fields.name: chunk_size
fields.doc: max XFER_DATA payload bytes the FC will use (<= 247)

fields.name: mtime
fields.doc: file mtime (epoch s) if known, else 0; ABI-safe extension

messages.name: XFER_DATA
messages.doc: One offset-addressed chunk on a bulk-transfer session, in either direction (download FC->GCS, upload GCS->FC). The receiver trusts `len`, never the unpacked `data` tail — the final short chunk trailing-zero-truncates on the wire (like SYSID_SAMPLE). flags carries EOF on the last chunk. Wire size 254 B (1 B under the 255 cap). docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md.

fields.name: len
fields.doc: valid bytes in data[] (authoritative; do not infer from the array)

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: byte offset of data[0] within the transfer

messages.name: XFER_ACK
messages.doc: Cumulative flow-control ack on a bulk-transfer session, in either direction. next_offset is the lowest byte offset NOT yet received (download: GCS->FC; upload: FC->GCS); the sender rewinds its cursor to next_offset to resume/refill (idempotent re-read). flags=NAK forces a rewind, DONE/ABORT terminate. docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: terminal result on DONE/ABORT, else ACCEPTED

fields.name: next_offset
fields.doc: lowest byte offset not yet received

messages.name: FS_ENTRY
messages.doc: One directory entry streamed in reply to FS_LIST (filesystem navigation). The FC emits one per entry (index 0..count-1) then a terminal entry with an empty name marking end-of-listing; on a bad/absent path it emits a single entry with result=DENIED and count=0. result=ACCEPTED on valid entries. docs/reference/messages/fs_nav.md.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: ACCEPTED ok; DENIED = path does not exist

fields.name: count
fields.doc: total entries (set on the terminal entry; 0 when not yet known)

messages.name: FS_INFO_REPLY
messages.doc: Status of one path, in reply to FS_INFO (filesystem navigation). result=ACCEPTED if the path exists (type/size/mtime valid), DENIED if it does not exist. docs/reference/messages/fs_nav.md.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: ACCEPTED = exists; DENIED = does not exist

fields.name: mtime
fields.doc: FatFS packed mtime if known, else 0

messages.name: NOTCH_STATUS
messages.doc: Live center frequencies of the FFT-driven dynamic gyro notch (dsp/gyro_notch), per axis, up to 3 notches each. 0 Hz = that slot is bypassed. enabled reflects the master gate (not the throttle gate).

messages.name: HSL_STATUS
messages.doc: High-speed IMU-to-SD stream (storage/imu_hs_log) status, so the recorder can be checked over the link instead of by pulling the card. Streamed at 1 Hz. dropped_sectors is the field that matters in flight: it is non-zero only when the card cannot sustain the write rate, and the samples it counts are gone.

fields.name: session
fields.doc: armed-period counter, monotonic for the life of the file

fields.name: head_slot
fields.doc: ring slot the next sector goes to

fields.name: ring_sectors
fields.doc: total ring slots; with head_slot and wraps this says how much of the ring holds data

fields.name: wraps
fields.doc: times the ring has been round since the file was created

fields.name: dropped_sectors
fields.doc: sectors lost because a stream's buffers filled before the FS task drained them, i.e. the card fell behind

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: seq the next frame will carry; its rate of change is the true sector rate

messages.name: CMD_ARM
messages.doc: Set the software-arm latch. Opens with the standard command header (spec §12.1).

messages.name: CMD_DISARM
messages.doc: Clear the software-arm latch.

messages.name: CMD_CALIBRATE_IMU
messages.doc: Start IMU calibration; progress streams back via CALIBRATION_STATUS.

messages.name: CMD_SET_PID
messages.doc: Set a PID gain set. v1 carries controller+axis+kp+ki+kd+kff.

messages.name: CMD_SET_GYRO_LPF
messages.doc: Set rate-loop gyro low-pass time constant per axis. v1: rc (seconds); <=0 disables.

messages.name: CMD_SET_D_LPF
messages.doc: Set rate-loop derivative (D-term) low-pass time constant per axis. v1: rc (seconds); <=0 disables filtering (raw D).

messages.name: CMD_SET_GYRO_NOTCH
messages.doc: Configure the FFT-driven dynamic gyro notch (dsp/gyro_notch): master enable plus the detection parameters, applied to all axes. A detection field <=0 leaves that parameter unchanged. Persisted to SD (pid.bin).

fields.name: min_ratio
fields.doc: peak prominence gate (x mean power); <=0 = unchanged

fields.name: autoband
fields.doc: 1 = arm a one-shot auto-band learn: characterise the hover spectrum and tighten [fmin,fmax] around it (live-only). 0 = no-op

messages.name: CMD_SET_MOTOR_GEOMETRY
messages.doc: Reconfigure the 4-motor mixer from per-motor position and spin direction. Persisted to SD (pid.bin) so the mixer layout survives a reboot.

messages.name: CMD_SET_FLIGHT_MODE
messages.doc: Override the flight mode (sticky GCS control, or release back to RC).

messages.name: CMD_SYSID_EXCITE
messages.doc: On-hardware system-ID: inject a linear chirp into one rate axis for `duration_s`, for plant identification on a rig. axis 0=roll/1=pitch/2=yaw; axis 0xFF aborts. `mode` selects the injection point: 0=rate SETPOINT (amp in deg/s; closed-loop, default) or 1=rate-PID OUTPUT u (amp in control-effort units; near-open-loop, more aggressive, tighter amp cap). The FC self-aborts on angle/rate limits. Phase 0: testable disarmed (motors stay off). `mode` is appended last so a sender that omits it (trailing-zero-truncated) gets mode 0.

messages.name: CMD_SYSID_DUMP
messages.doc: Request the FC stream back the last CMD_SYSID_EXCITE capture buffer as SYSID_SAMPLE chunks. Idempotent — re-send to re-dump (e.g. to fill dropped chunks).

messages.name: XFER_OPEN
messages.doc: Open a bulk-transfer/stream session on the generic xfer substrate (docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md). The FC replies with COMMAND_ACK (deferred) then XFER_INFO. dir 0=download (FC->GCS), 1=upload (GCS->FC). mode 0=file, 1=stream (rate_hz applies; total_size advertised 0xFFFFFFFF). service_id selects the provider (0=file,1=log,2=stream); arg is the provider argument (e.g. SD path or stream name). Re-send with the same (session,req_seq) is idempotent.

fields.name: rate_hz
fields.doc: stream mode emission rate; 0 in file mode

messages.name: XFER_CLOSE
messages.doc: Close/abort a bulk-transfer session (docs/plans/navlink-xfer-substrate.md). The FC tears down the session, calls provider close, and ACKs. result records the GCS-side reason (ACCEPTED = normal completion).

messages.name: FS_LIST
messages.doc: List the files/folders in a directory (filesystem navigation). The FC replies with COMMAND_ACK (deferred) then a stream of FS_ENTRY. If the path does not exist a single FS_ENTRY with result=DENIED is returned. start_index lets the GCS resume/refill from a given entry. docs/reference/messages/fs_nav.md.

fields.name: start_index
fields.doc: first entry index to emit (resume point)

messages.name: FS_INFO
messages.doc: Request the status of a single path (filesystem navigation). The FC replies with COMMAND_ACK (deferred) then FS_INFO_REPLY (result=DENIED if the path does not exist). docs/reference/messages/fs_nav.md.

messages.name: PARAM_REQUEST_LIST
messages.doc: Request a full parameter dump (spec §12.2).

messages.name: PARAM_REQUEST_READ
messages.doc: Request one parameter by name (index=-1) or by index (spec §12.2).

messages.name: PARAM_VALUE
messages.doc: Typed parameter value (spec §12.2). 'value' is the real type, never a float bit-cast.

messages.name: PARAM_SET
messages.doc: Write one parameter; answered by the updated PARAM_VALUE (spec §12.2).

messages.name: CALIBRATION_STATUS
messages.doc: IMU calibration progress + operator instruction. Drives the GCS calibration wizard (spec §14.8). The terminal COMPLETE/FAILED steps tell the wizard the routine ended; it no longer infers completion from a STANDBY heartbeat (which never arrives if calibration legitimately ends in FAILSAFE).

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: 0..100 percent for PROGRESS; reason code for FAILED; 0 otherwise

fields.name: coverage
fields.doc: mag axis coverage x/y/z for MAG_AXIS_COVERAGE; 0 otherwise

messages.name: HW_TEST_BEGIN
messages.doc: On-hardware bench suite starting. Test-only (hwtest firmware); vendor/test msgid range 0x800000+, emitted only under generate.py --profile test. See firmware/docs/plans/on-hardware-test-and-coverage.md.

messages.name: HW_TEST_RESULT
messages.doc: One on-hardware bench check result. Test-only (hwtest firmware).

messages.name: HW_TEST_DONE
messages.doc: On-hardware bench suite finished. Test-only (hwtest firmware).
